content: 1. Stakeholders should adopt best practices derived from the operations, performance, and contributions of competent research institutes and agencies involved in health intervention and technology assessment. These experiences should be shared with Member States through appropriate channels and activities, including global and regional networks and academic institutions. 2. The integration of health intervention and technology assessment concepts and principles into relevant WHO strategies and areas of work is essential. This includes, but is not limited to, areas such as universal health coverage, health financing, access to and rational use of quality-assured medicines, vaccines, and other health technologies, prevention and management of noncommunicable and communicable diseases, maternal and child care, and the formulation of evidence-based health policies. 3. Technical support should be provided to Member States, particularly low-income countries, as well as relevant intergovernmental organizations and global health partners. This support aims to strengthen their capacity for health intervention and technology assessment, including the development and use of global guidance on methods and processes based on internationally agreed practices, where appropriate. 4. WHO must ensure adequate capacity at all levels by utilizing its networks of experts and collaborating centers, as well as other regional and international networks. This is necessary to meet the demand for support in facilitating evidence-based policy decisions in Member States. 5. The exchange of information, sharing of experiences, and capacity-building in health intervention and technology assessment should be supported through collaborative mechanisms and networks at global, regional, and country levels. These partnerships must be active, effective, and sustainable. 6. Progress in implementing this resolution should be reported to the Sixty-ninth World Health Assembly.
